page_title: argparse — Parser for command-line options, arguments and subcommands

sources.entry: argparse - (Python standard library) Command-line option and argument parsing.

summary.name: argparse
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module for building user-friendly command-line interfaces, parsing sys.argv into named arguments and generating help and usage messages.
use_cases: building a command-line tool in Python
generating help and usage text automatically
sharing common arguments across several parsers
migrating optparse code to a modern parser
summary.what_it_does: The argparse module provides ArgumentParser, which defines the arguments a program accepts via add_argument() (positional arguments, options taking values, and on/off flags) and parses them with parse_args() into a Namespace object. It automatically generates help and usage messages and reports errors for invalid input. The page documents many options, including prog, usage, description, epilog, parents for sharing arguments, formatter_class variants for help formatting, prefix_chars, fromfile_prefix_chars for reading arguments from a file, argument_default, allow_abbrev, conflict_handler, add_help, exit_on_error, suggest_on_error, and color. The page is the API reference, with code examples throughout.
notable: Part of the Python standard library, so no installation is needed
Automatically generates help and usage messages
Supports parent parsers to share argument definitions
Can read additional arguments from files via fromfile_prefix_chars
caveats: The page notes argparse may lack control for some behaviors, such as disabling interspersed options or accepting values that start with '-'; alternatives are listed in 'Choosing an argument parsing library'.
Some features are version-specific (e.g., suggest_on_error and color added in 3.14, suggest_on_error default changed in 3.15).
